meta.titre: Refrigerator and Freezer Use: Storing Food Safely and Buying Wisely
meta.sous_theme: Temperatures, correct use, quick freezing, thawing and buying a freezer

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Food and Nutrition past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: When the electricity returns after a long power cut, many families open the freezer and find the meat soft and the fish smelling. A refrigerator or a freezer is one of the costliest items in a home, and it only protects food when it is chosen, loaded and used correctly. The GCE asks how cold keeps food, how to use these appliances, and what to look for when buying one.

items: Bacteria and moulds grow quickly in warm, moist conditions.
Low temperatures slow the growth of micro-organisms.

sections.titre: Using the refrigerator and the freezer
sections.contenu_markdown:
### How cold keeps food
Micro-organisms grow slowly in the cold. A refrigerator keeps food between about 0 °C and 5 °C: bacteria grow slowly but are not killed, so food keeps for days only. A freezer keeps food at -18 °C or colder: micro-organisms become inactive but are not killed, so food keeps for months and the bacteria grow again when the food warms.

### Using the refrigerator
- Cool hot food quickly before putting it in; cover all food.
- Keep raw meat and fish on the lowest shelf, covered, so that juices cannot drip onto other foods.
- Do not overfill: air must circulate.
- Keep the door shut. The door is the warmest part because it is opened often and warm air enters. Temperatures also differ between shelves, and the coolest shelf depends on the model, so read the instructions.
- Clean it often, defrost it if it is not frost-free, and use older food first.

### Using the freezer
- Freeze only fresh food in good condition, in small portions, wrapped in airtight containers or freezer bags and labelled with the date.
- Blanch vegetables before freezing.
- Freeze food quickly. Quick freezing makes small ice crystals that damage the food cells little, so the food keeps its texture. Slow freezing makes large ice crystals that burst cells, and the food becomes soft and watery when thawed.
- Air that touches the surface dries the food and leaves grey patches (freezer burn); wrap food tightly.
- Thaw food completely in the refrigerator and cook it soon after. Do not refreeze raw food that has thawed.
- During a power cut keep the door closed.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for points to consider before buying a freezer.
variantes.contenu_markdown:
1. Size or capacity that fits the family and the way it shops.
2. Type (chest or upright) and the floor space available.
3. Running cost: electricity used.
4. Price, guarantee, and after-sales service and spare parts.
5. Reputation of the make.
6. Useful features: adjustable thermostat, fast-freeze switch, lock, warning light, easy cleaning.
7. Reliable electricity supply in the home.
Give the exact number of guidelines asked for and a short reason for each.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked how to avoid food poisoning when chilling, freezing or thawing food.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Cool cooked food fast and refrigerate it soon; eat leftovers within a short time. Thaw frozen meat and fish in the refrigerator, not on the kitchen counter, because the outside warms while the middle is still frozen. Cook thawed food soon and cook it right through. Food cooked from raw can be frozen again after cooking, but raw food that has thawed should not be refrozen.

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain why food that is frozen quickly keeps its quality better than food that is frozen slowly, and state three rules for packing food for the freezer. (5 marks)

etapes.action: Read the command words and the marks.
etapes.justification: "Explain" asks for a reason, and "state" asks for three short rules; 5 marks suggest 2 marks for the explanation and 3 for the rules.
etapes.resultat_markdown: An explanation of two linked points, then exactly three rules.

etapes.action: Explain the effect of freezing speed.
etapes.justification: The size of the ice crystals depends on how fast the food freezes.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Quick freezing makes small ice crystals that do little damage to the food cells; slow freezing makes large crystals that burst cells, so thawed food is soft and loses liquid.

etapes.justification: Packing protects food from air and helps with storage.
etapes.resultat_markdown: 1. Wrap in airtight containers or freezer bags to prevent freezer burn. 2. Pack in small portions so that only the needed amount is thawed. 3. Label with the contents and the date.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Quick freezing forms small ice crystals that do not burst the cells, so the food keeps its texture and does not become watery when it thaws, while slow freezing forms large crystals that rupture the cells. Packing rules: wrap food airtight; freeze small portions; label with contents and date.

items.erreur_markdown: "The freezer kills the bacteria in the food."
items.pourquoi_faux: Freezing only makes bacteria inactive. When the food thaws they grow again.
items.correction_markdown: Say that freezing stops the growth of bacteria but does not kill them, so thawed food must be cooked and eaten soon.

items.erreur_markdown: Putting a large pot of hot stew straight into the refrigerator.
items.pourquoi_faux: It warms the other food and the stew itself cools too slowly in the middle, so bacteria can grow.
items.correction_markdown: Cool the food quickly first, in small shallow containers, then cover and refrigerate.

items.erreur_markdown: Thawing frozen chicken on the kitchen table overnight.
items.pourquoi_faux: The outside becomes warm enough for bacteria to multiply long before the centre thaws.
items.correction_markdown: Thaw it completely in the refrigerator, then cook it soon after.

items.erreur_markdown: Describing large ice crystals as a sign of good, quick freezing.
items.pourquoi_faux: Large crystals form during slow freezing and burst food cells; quick freezing gives small crystals.
items.correction_markdown: Quick freezing: small ice crystals; slow freezing: large ice crystals.

items.erreur_markdown: Opening the freezer door often during a power cut to check on the food.
items.pourquoi_faux: Each opening lets warm air in and the food thaws sooner.
items.correction_markdown: Keep the door closed so the cold is kept in as long as possible.

items.enonce_markdown: State (a) the temperature at which a freezer should store food, (b) the usual temperature range inside a refrigerator, (c) the best place for raw meat in a refrigerator, and (d) what must be done to hot food before it is put in the refrigerator.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **-18 °C or colder**. (b) **about 0 °C to 5 °C**. (c) **On the lowest shelf, covered**, so that juices cannot drip on other food. (d) **It must be cooled quickly** (and covered).

items.enonce_markdown: Refrigerator A uses 1.2 kWh of electricity a day. Refrigerator B uses 0.9 kWh a day. Electricity costs 75 FCFA per kWh (an assumed price). Take a month as 30 days. (a) Find the monthly cost of running each one. (b) Find how much is saved in a year by buying B. (c) Give one other point to check before buying a refrigerator.
items.solution_markdown: (a) A: $1.2 \times 30 = 36$ kWh, and $36 \times 75 = 2\,700$, so **$2\,700$ FCFA**. B: $0.9 \times 30 = 27$ kWh, and $27 \times 75 = 2\,025$, so **$2\,025$ FCFA**. (b) Monthly saving: $2\,700 - 2\,025 = 675$. Yearly saving: $675 \times 12 = 8\,100$, so **$8\,100$ FCFA**. (c) Any one of: capacity for the family; price and guarantee; after-sales service; space in the kitchen; features such as an adjustable thermostat.

items.enonce_markdown: A power cut lasts a whole day and a family has a full freezer. (a) State three actions that help the food to stay frozen. (b) The next day the electricity returns. Some pieces of raw chicken have thawed completely and are warm. What should be done with them and why? (c) Explain why thawed raw chicken should not simply be put back in the freezer.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Any three of: keep the door closed; cover the freezer with blankets for insulation; do not put in new warm food; group packs together; use a generator or other power supply if available. (b) **Throw them away** if they have been warm for a long time, because bacteria will have multiplied. (c) Bacteria that grew while the food was warm are not killed by freezing, and when the chicken is thawed again the numbers can be high enough to cause food poisoning. Food that is still cold with ice crystals can be cooked and the cooked dish frozen.

items_markdown: Refrigerator: about 0 °C to 5 °C, slows bacteria for days. Freezer: -18 °C or colder, keeps food for months; neither kills bacteria.
Quick freezing gives small ice crystals and good texture; slow freezing gives large crystals that burst cells.
Fridge rules: cool and cover food, raw meat on the lowest shelf, do not overfill, keep the door shut, clean and defrost.
Freezer rules: fresh food, small airtight labelled packs, blanch vegetables, thaw in the refrigerator, do not refreeze raw thawed food.
Buying a freezer: capacity, type and space, running cost, price and guarantee, service, make, features.
Running cost = kWh used × price per kWh; recalculate carefully and give the unit.
